title: DevTooling Runway & Commitment Ledger — initiative tracking for SDKs, docs, and quickstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build a lightweight, repeatable ledger for tracking commitments and outcomes for the Developer Tooling initiative (SDKs, docs, quickstarts, sample apps). Problem: current initiative tracking is fragmented across spreadsheets, Notion pages, and ad-hoc Slack updates — team velocity and OKR alignment are hard to measure. Goal: deliver a single-source 'Commitment Ledger' + cadence that surfaces owner commitments, signal-based progress, risk heatmap, and quarterly roll-ups for leadership.

Scope: capture each initiative chunk (e.g., SDK language bindings, quickstart recipes, sample app cohorts) as a ledger row with: owner, commit (deliverable + acceptance), timebox, leading signals (activation, first-call success, 7-day retention of sample projects), lagging signals (adoption, support tickets), blockers, and mitigation plan. Ledger will power a weekly operational snapshot and a monthly OKR roll-up.

Success metrics: 1) 80% of active initiatives have a committed owner + acceptance criteria in ledger; 2) reduce untriaged devx support tickets related to quickstarts by 30% in quarter; 3) time-to-first-call median <= 10 minutes on guided quickstarts; 4) clear risk heatmap with actions for all 'high' risks.

Approach: 1) prototype ledger schema in Notion and a companion CSV export; 2) instrument signals pipeline (Activation API + analytics) to populate leading metrics automatically into the ledger; 3) create a weekly cadence: owners update progress + blockers; PM synthesizes heatmap and escalates engineering dependencies; 4) embed the ledger view into the monthly OKR readout and the DevX portal.

Trade-offs & decisions to date: choose minimal viable schema to avoid heavy process overhead; prefer signal automation over manual status where feasible (to reduce bias); accept initial manual curation for qualitative notes.

Acceptance criteria: ledger exists in Notion with at least 12 active rows representing priority SDKs/quickstarts, signal pipeline emits weekly activation numbers for 75% of rows, and first heatmap presented to leadership in June review.

Next steps: finalize schema (PM + Eng infra), build data hooks (ENG-4211), onboard owners and pilot 6 initiatives for April sprint.
